newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hijacked cargo ship back in Singapore - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hijacked cargo ship back in Singapore - paper.

text.p: A hijacked Belize-registered cargo ship and its 13 crew, held for six days by pirates off Malaysia, has arrived back in Singapore, the Straits Times newspaper reported on Friday.
"My men are really glad to be back in Singapore safely. For them it is like being given back their lives," Foo Say Yuen, owner of the MV Wint Thai, was quoted as saying.

The ship was boarded early on March 5 by about 10 gun-toting pirates who fired shots, handcuffed the crew and beat them with rifles before stealing a consignment of cigarettes worth Singapore $5 million (US$3.5 million).
The vessel was on its way to South Korea from Singapore.

The alarm was raised on Tuesday after the vessel was released and the crew used the one radio set not smashed or taken by the pirates to alert officials at the International Maritime Bureau Piracy Centre in Kuala Lumpur.
The ship, which anchored off Sentosa Island on Thursday, was quarantined by Singapore immigration officials. The pirates had also stolen the passports of the mainly Burmese and Indonesian crew.
Three crew injured in the ordeal in the South China Sea were taken to Singapore General Hospital for treatment after the MV Wint Thai docked.
The injured men needed treatment for a gunshot wound, a severe gash and a facial laceration, the report said.
